title: Decouple test from doctor's repository health reporting
context: Test was asserting doctor exits with status 0, but doctor correctly exits 1 when a release commit's npm pins cannot be served yet. This health reporting is unrelated to what the test measures: CLI execution and cache isolation. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Remove the exit-status equality check. Replace with assertions that directly measure the test's actual concerns: CLI ran (verified via stdout), no user cache was created (file doesn't exist). Check only that status is a number, not that it equals 0.
consequences: Test no longer fails on unrelated doctor health issues
Test assertions now directly reflect stated purpose
Reduces brittleness to future changes in repo health checks
Intent is explicit for future maintainers
alternatives_rejected: Skip test during release commits (masks the real concern, doesn't fix design)
Mock doctor's exit status (incorrect—the exit 1 is valid health reporting)
Accept flaky behavior (test becomes unreliable as health checks evolve)
